scores.proposal: decisive: Relayed inner-discovery prior (design r) with an on/off-policy, chain-replicated held-out test
fatal_flaws: Nothing fatal statistically. The weakness is the prior on the effect: the expected effect (+0.002) is below the detectable 0.006 to 0.007, and the proposal itself puts P(E-R1) at about 0.1. The inner search measured -0.002/-0.003 against o0. A per-cell prior mostly moves variant slots away from cells that the two-batch rule already rejects, so the likely product is an upper bound on one simple mechanism, not a discovery.

The recursion is a hand-written per-cell prior (adaptive operator selection carried across tasks). The learning principle is not searched, and there is no 'retains skills' arm. Novelty against instructions 12 to 14 is low.

tau = 0.008 is a planning value with no measured basis. My check gives power at 0.007 of 0.64 at tau 0.012 and 0.46 at tau 0.015. The CPU of the fresh categories at train 200 is unknown, so the size rule may lower their budget. designs.py is pinned by registration_o.
The inner 'acceptances' (about 60 switches per chain) carry no false-acceptance control; q's switches were mostly noise. Only the claim-level test is controlled.
best_parts: Every power number checks: SE 0.0019 over 32 chain means, critical mean 0.0047 at t(31) = 2.45, power 0.18/0.55/0.88/1.00, 90% power at 0.0072 (0.0062/0.0085 at sigma 0.02/0.04), secondaries 90% at 0.0088, futility stop 0.69 under the null and 0.02 at 0.007.

The replication unit is the chain (32 independent meta-trainings), with tau in the variance. Primary alpha 0.01, gated Holm secondaries, non-binding futility look, and alpha spending across further attempts.

The recursion is exercised in every acquisition, unlike designs that need an accepted change of principle. Three controls separate the explanations: shuffled labels (peakedness), off-policy memory (recursion versus accumulation) and frozen@4B (a ceiling that names the limit of a negative).

It reads the code correctly: untrained answers are identical, so min(delta) equals delta-acquired; the training split ignores the seed; Cache returns no memory; design o has eight distinct lineages (recursive = frozen).
scores.justification: Under the power and statistics lens this is the only proposal whose recursion test is both always exercised and adequately powered. I checked every number in its power analysis and in its CPU arithmetic (about 175,000 CPU-s including development). False acceptance is controlled at the claim level (0.01, with family-wise and cross-attempt spending), and the negative region is pre-defined, with diagnostics (L1 to L5) that locate the cause. Its own numbers say the most probable outcome is a decisive negative about a mechanism of low novelty, and one planning input (tau) is unmeasured. It mislabels budget_scaling's edit-noise figure as o0's noise. Like every proposal, it defines no m_net.

scores.proposal: statistics: Race-and-panel acceptance (noise-allocated SPRT screening, known-variance confirmation)
fatal_flaws: The recursion test is probably empty. R and F share every race run until a change of learning principle is accepted, and the principle cells screened harmful (propose/replace -0.040, init/mutarg -0.020). E3(a) is predicted to fail and R - F is about 0 by construction. The design certifies source acceptances, not recursion.

The race and the panel both use part A. A seed changes only relabelling and draws, never the instances, and environment.split ignores the seed, so the same 12 training problems are used every time. Fresh seeds remove the learner-noise winner's curse but not instance-level selection, so SE 0.0015 certifies an instance-conditional effect. Its own M3 prediction is -0.002 per accepted step on the held-out categories.

Its effect-distribution scenarios (0.2 versus 3.4 acceptances per lineage) are fitted to duplicated data. Three of the four confirmations are one candidate, and the recursive and frozen lineages are identical. The fitted mean shares one o0 run per category on seed 61, whose own deviation has an sd of about 0.008.
best_parts: Information per CPU-second checks: 0.0072 for the registered layout, 0.0036 without knapsack, 0.0016 at 8:3:1 (Neyman optimum 0.0015). Cycle SE 0.0064, panel SE 0.0015 (686 CPU-s at run-budget CPU), so the smallest accepted mean falls from 0.0179 to 0.0039 in 3-category units.

False acceptance is tightly controlled: alpha 0.005 per confirmation on a panel independent of the race, a no-harm condition per category, max(1.1 x pooled, own) variance, a non-binding futility look, a Bonferroni bound of 0.10 per lineage, and 0.014 per lineage in its worst-case simulation.
It drops knapsack (exact-zero pairs, about 50% of CPU), feeds the discoverer shrunken estimates instead of one-seed screens, and adds a per-step transfer endpoint (M3).
Its rho analysis is correct, k = 3rho/(1+2rho), with values -0.005/0.000/+0.004 at rho 0/0.2/0.5. It states plainly that it is not a new principle.
scores.justification: This is the best-engineered acceptance machine. Its statistics are standard, correct and checkable. It would plausibly produce some source acceptances (about 1 per lineage) with a false-acceptance rate far below the registered rule's. Under the lens it falls short on the recursion: in the likely case no change of principle is accepted, and R and F are then the same process. Its calibration also inherits duplicated and offset-confounded inputs from design o's ledger. Minor issues: 8:3:1 is a rounded allocation, not the Neyman ratio (about 15:5:1), the CPU totals are about 2,500 off its own table, and m_net is not defined. It is orthogonal to the others and could serve as their acceptance layer.

scores.proposal: generator: PEM pooled posterior of edit effects, threshold-sized macro-edits, generator tested on fresh categories
fatal_flaws: The acceptance forecast (0.18 pass per step, about 8 per arm) is analytic and not simulated. It rests on a single-edit true sd of 0.004 inferred from r = 0.10 over 66 promoted candidates, about 12 to 15 of them duplicates; that r has an SE of about 0.14, which allows any sd from 0 to 0.007. It also assumes additive edits and a kept-edit mean of 0 or more. budget_scaling found 4 of 8 single edits gave identical runs, so a k = 8 macro may hold about 4 effective edits (pass probability about 0.1).

G_R0, knowledge-free K = 8 macros, is predicted at -0.05, so the G* - G_R0 part of E_meta is close to automatic. There is no control with knowledge-free macros restricted to the non-destructive cells, so 'what was discovered' may reduce to a list of destructive cells.

P5 puts Y1(G*) at +0.005 on part B of unseen categories, above every confirmed effect measured so far (+0.0012 on the same instances). The 0.6 probability for E_meta is overconfident. The meta stage is void if the fresh categories cost much more than 10 s per run (E < 12).
Pooling R's four lineages into one posterior leaves the recursive arm without independent replication on the source categories.
best_parts: It correctly identifies that every lineage of design o screened against the same o0 runs (seeds 61 to 63), and gives each lineage its own seeds.

It sizes candidates to the measured detection limit. My checks agree: SE 0.0056, 50% power at 0.0147, F's expected 0.0035 acceptances per step, pass probability Phi(-0.92) = 0.18 under its assumptions.

The recursion is exercised at every step through the pooled posterior. The frozen generator itself is tested on unseen categories in paired, compute-matched one-step episodes confirmed on part B: SE 0.0019, 80% power at 0.0047.
Leakage controls are good: predictions are recorded before each run, and confirmation data enter the model only after the decision.
scores.justification: It is the most direct test of whether discoveries transform the generator. It measures this on unseen categories and confirms on new instance groups, which is better than the part-A confirmations of the others. Under the lens its power is conditional: the source-acceptance argument is a chain of approximations from fragile, partly duplicated estimates, and one of the three E_meta parts is near-guaranteed by a weak control. False acceptance stays at about 1% per confirmation under the registered rule, though macros change the noise profile, so the rule must be recalibrated (D4 is planned). The CPU arithmetic checks (at most 209,000). The success odds are overstated, and m_net is not defined.

scores.proposal: unconventional: Self-model discovery (k-NN surrogate of the learner's own acquisition landscape, refit by adopted principles)
fatal_flaws: Acceptances depend on fidelity in the upper tail. Taking the argmax over about 1,000 simulated candidates on a sparse table (4,000 directions in about 8 effective dimensions, one relabelling, no test-time local improvement) selects surrogate errors. The go/no-go check D4 (Spearman over 24 random W-cell mechanisms) can pass on destructive edits alone, since harm is easy to predict, even when fidelity among improvements is about 0.

The assumed N(-0.002, 0.006) for W-cell effects overstates the upper tail. The data imply a non-destructive true sd of about 0.003 to 0.004, plus a harmful skew. At sd 0.0035 and rho 0.5 the expected best is about +0.0036, which passes the gate with probability about 0.15, not 0.65.

The recursion is likely not exercised (it states P 0.35; the principle cells screened harmful). The real recursion contrasts are powered only above about 0.008, and S1 runs inside the simulator. score/pick are frozen, so instruction 14's joint evolution of representation and discovery operators is not tested.
best_parts: Selection happens in the simulator and confirmation on real seeds used for nothing else, so confirmed means are unbiased.
The stratified 16-seed gate checks out: SE 0.0028, smallest accepted mean 0.0065, power 0.18/0.42/0.70/0.89/0.99, 1% per confirmation and at most 5% per lineage.

Its negative control and development checks are sound. W-shuffled is an empirical check of the false-acceptance rate. D1 is an exact replay test of the simulator against real acquisition. D2 and D4 are pre-registration gates that stop the technique and record the negative. The block-normalised table is exact for generation 0's linear programs.
It changes no pinned file (its products are design-o versions) and reads no reference while building tables.
scores.justification: The measurement layer is strong: unbiased confirmation and a controlled gate, with go/no-go checks before any registered compute is spent. Its power to produce acceptances is a bet on surrogate fidelity, and its effect-size input is optimistic. The recursion is probably unexercised, and where exercised it is mainly tested inside the simulator. Under the lens it would most likely end at D4, or with few real acceptances and no measurable recursion. It misstates the held-out H1 power: 0.90 is the power of the '> 0' part only, and the point-estimate condition >= 0.01 holds about half the time at a true 0.01. It is candid about not being radical, and it defines no m_net.

scores.proposal: level: Design r, recursive discovery inside acquisition with an amortised cross-category discoverer
fatal_flaws: The recursion across categories (amortised w0, L0, m0 and principle) rests on two independent chains. By its own numbers, R - Z is detectable only from +0.007 to +0.008 against an expected +0.003 (power about 0.15). E1r has power about 0.25, and adoption about 0.2 to 0.9 per chain. It predicts the success condition fails with probability at least 0.9.

No false-acceptance rate is derived for in-run acceptance. The screened best of six is confirmed with at least 4 of 6 wins on 6 training problems, and that win criterion alone passes a null candidate with probability 0.34. Noise-driven switches, as in q, are likely to dominate; the final check only bounds the loss.

Runs cost about 12 times the registered CPU, so the held-out stage needs 70,000 to 140,000 CPU-s or more depending on unknown fresh-category costs. designs.py is pinned. n_train 24 may exceed some training pools.
best_parts: It removes dilution across categories: effects are judged within one category, at about 2 CPU-s per candidate against about 100 s per candidate in design o.
Every candidate gets an equal learning round with common draws and is judged by the post-improvement answer. Untrained answers are identical, so the min statistic equals the change of acquired.

It maps the directive's five comparisons explicitly: Z (reset), K (skills only), F (frozen principle), O@R and Q@R (compute and inner search without discovery), with raise_until matching and void rules.
The unit and CPU arithmetic checks: 9,600 units per run, 610 per step, 15 steps, 75,000 source CPU-s, 17,500 per cheap held-out category.
scores.justification: The idea is sound and the controls follow the directive, but this is the weakest proposal under the lens. The decisions that drive the recursion are made on 6 + 6 training problems with no derived false-acceptance control. The recursion it would claim is replicated by two chains, and every endpoint it cares about has power of 0.15 to 0.25 at the effects it expects. It pools q's two switch rules into '49 of 112'; the two-batch rule alone gave 15 of 62. It also overstates that every held-out run replicates the whole recursive process. m_net is not defined.

errors_in_proposals: statistics, generator: they treat '4 confirmations in 29 steps' and '+0.0089 -> +0.0012' as independent calibration data. diagnose_open_discovery.json (confirmation_rows) shows recursive0, frozen0 and shuffled0 confirming the same step-0 candidate (screen 0.003995, promoted 0.009663; confirmed -0.0080, +0.0015, +0.0042 on different seeds). recursive1 and frozen1 are identical (both spent 1149.049): recursive and frozen are the same process until a change of principle. That leaves 2 distinct confirmed candidates and about 22 distinct steps. The 66 promoted pairs behind r = 0.10 include about 12 to 15 duplicates.

statistics, generator, unconventional: the location of the mild-edit effect distribution (screen mean -0.0088; fits at -0.008/-0.005; 'kept edits +/-0.001'; 'W-cell mean -0.002') is not identified. registration_o gives every lineage the discovery seeds [61, 62, 63], and no step was accepted, so all 174 screening values subtract the same o0 run per category on seed 61. From the paired sds (0.021, 0.039, 0.006), that parent run's own deviation has an sd of about 0.008 on the 4-category screen mean and about 0.0056 on the 2-seed promotion mean. That is as large as the measured mean and as the 0.0089 -> 0.0012 shrinkage. Only 'generator' flags this offset.

statistics: '8:3:1 ... the Neyman allocation ... recomputed from the measured sd/sqrt(cpu)' is not what the data give. With paired sd (0.039, 0.021, 0.006) and CPU per run (1.8, 5.0, 9.2), sigma/sqrt(c) gives QAP:JS:PM of about 14.7:4.7:1. 8:3:1 gives var x CPU 0.00160 against the optimum 0.00153, so it is about 4.5 times, not 4.8 times, better than the registered 0.0072. Its total line (198,000 to 228,000) is about 2,500 below its own table (200,500 to 230,500).

level: 'q with a weaker rule switched in 49 of 112 program rounds' pools two rules. q_compare1.txt (one-batch rule) has 34 switches in 50 program rounds; q_compare2.txt (two-batch rule) has 15 in 62. Also, 'Promoted candidates were worth +0.0012 on the confirmation seeds': +0.0012 is the mean of the 4 confirmations (2 distinct candidates), not of the promoted candidates.

level: 'In-run false acceptance targeted at <= 5% per step ... at most 0.75 false' per run is not supported. The stated rule confirms the screened best of six with at least 4 of 6 wins on 6 problems. P(>= 4 of 6 | p = 0.5) = 22/64 = 0.34 for the win condition alone, and nothing in the design brings the per-step rate to 5%.

level: 'Every held-out run then becomes an independent replicate of the whole recursive process' is overstated. The cross-generation state (w0, L0, m0, principle) comes from two chains only (R1 used on H1-8, R2 on H9-16). Held-out seeds replicate the in-run process, not the amortisation.

unconventional: held-out 'power 0.90 for 0.01' is overstated. H1 requires a point estimate of at least 0.01, a lower bound above 0, and no category below -0.005. At a true 0.01 the point-estimate condition alone holds about 50% of the time; 0.90 is the power of the '> 0' condition only.

unconventional: 'about 100 CPU-s for one candidate evaluation in design o's kernel screening' is wrong. A screen is 1 seed x 4 categories at the search budget, about 22 to 32 CPU-s; about 100 s is a 400 to 800 CPU-s step divided by six candidates, including promotion and confirmation. Its '1,630 CPU-s per confirmation (51 s per mechanism-seed)' uses run-budget CPU (n_train 16, all fresh instances) for a part-A gate at the search budget, which costs about 0.7 times that. This error is conservative.

unconventional: 'real effects among principle and scalar edits have mean -0.002 and sd 0.006', so 'top of 1,000 = rho x 3.2 x 0.006 - 0.002', overstates the upper tail. The measured screen-promotion correlation of 0.10 implies a non-destructive true sd of about 0.003. The W cells' spread is a harmful tail (propose/replace -0.040, init/mutarg -0.020, propose/mutop -0.010) that does not raise the maximum. At sd 0.0035 and rho 0.5 the expected best is about +0.0036, which passes with probability about 0.15, not 0.65.

generator: 'single non-destructive edits have a true-effect sd of about 0.004', so 'sd 0.0113 at k = 8', is weakly supported. r = 0.10 over 66 promoted candidates, about 12 to 15 of them duplicates, has an SE of about 0.14, so the implied sd could be anywhere from 0 to about 0.007. budget_scaling.json reports that 4 of 8 single edits produced identical runs at both budgets even though their behaviour keys differed. A k = 8 macro may therefore hold about 4 effective edits (sd 0.008), giving a pass probability of about 0.1, not 0.18.

decisive: 'o0's noise on a 12-pair mean falls from 0.015 to 0.006 ... 1.6 times more precision per CPU-second' mislabels the figure. In budget_scaling.json, sd_of_a_12_pair_mean_from_noise is the noise of edit-minus-parent means over eight edits. It is heteroscedastic and dominated by p-median (sigma 0.088 -> 0.030, driven by the harmful score/replace edit), while job shop's sigma rose from 0.0068 to 0.0197. It is neither o0's own noise nor the relay - frozen noise. Also, 'at least one false acceptance has probability about 0.5 to 0.6' should be 0.49 to 0.67 (1 - 0.92^8 and 1 - 0.87^8), and those are worst-case per-lineage rates (every step confirming), while only 4 of 29 steps confirmed.
all five (an omission, not a numeric error): none states a definition of m_net, which instruction 14 requires and the brief says must be stated, and none has an explicit retention endpoint.
